metadata.case_name: LAM YIM FONG v. ADVARA INVESTMENT LTD

plaintiff.occupation_before: cashier of a money exchange company (Kinying Renminbi Exchange Co)
plaintiff.occupation_after: not in the labour market; caring for her daughter
plaintiff.education_level: secondary education in Hong Kong with little vocational training

source: The experts agree that the plaintiff had a mild head injury at the time when she was hit by the fallen signboard.

injuries.description: right shoulder injury (right shoulder pain and decreased movement)
source: she was taken to the Accident and Emergency Department of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital and the plaintiff complained of “right shoulder pain and decrease in movement”.
injuries.icd_description: Dislocation or strain or sprain of joints or ligaments of shoulder girdle, unspecified

injuries.description: vasovagal syncope (episode of dizziness and loss of consciousness)
source: She was discharged on 15 June 2010 with a diagnosis of vasovagal syncope.

injuries.description: post-concussional syndrome (as described by defendant's expert)
source: As a result of the accident, she complains of headache, dizziness and memory impairment which are consistent with the diagnosis of post-concussional syndrome.

manifestations.description: on and off headache described as like being jabbed by many needles; frequency ranges from every second day to 3 to 4 times a month, each bout lasting half a day to a few days
memory impairment: memorizing a new telephone number is now beyond her; cannot keep a shopping list in her mind; may forget where she has placed her belongings
persistent neck and right shoulder pain and stiffness, which increase after sleep in the morning, or with rainy and windy weather
brief vertigo induced by Barany maneuver (without nystagmus)
loss of consciousness for five minutes followed by sleepiness
moderate degree of diffuse give-way weakness in the right arm
insomnia (used to enjoy normal sleep but has become insomniac after the accident)
reduced ability to perform domestic chores because such duty as mopping the floor would induce vertigo
temper has got worse; she scolds her family members often

treatments_received.treatment: attendance and treatment at the Accident and Emergency Department of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital
source: She was taken to the Accident and Emergency Department of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital and the plaintiff complained of “right shoulder pain and decrease in movement”. An X-ray examination did not reveal any fracture. She was treated and discharged on the same day.
An X-ray examination did not reveal any fracture.

treatments_received.treatment: CT scan of the brain (no abnormality revealed)
source: A CT scan was conducted but no abnormality was discovered.
Another CT scan of her brain was conducted and again no abnormality was revealed.

treatments_received.treatment: admission to the Neurosurgical Ward of the Prince of Wales Hospital
source: on 7 June 2010 the plaintiff was eventually admitted to the Neurosurgical Ward of the Prince of Wales Hospital.

She was re-admitted to the Neurosurgical Ward of the Prince of Wales Hospital on 13 June 2010 after an episode of dizziness and loss of consciousness for five minutes which was followed by sleepiness.
The plaintiff was discharged “with reassurance” on 8 June 2010.
She was discharged on 15 June 2010 with a diagnosis of vasovagal syncope.

treatments_received.treatment: visits to bone setters and herbalist
source: The parties agree the plaintiff’s medical expenses, including those of bone setters and herbalist, at $6,000.

treatments_received.treatment: use of pain killers and plasters
source: The plaintiff is claiming $1,500 for pain killers/plasters and $8,000 for tonic food.
The plaintiff is claiming $1,500 for pain killers/plasters and $8,000 for tonic food.

losses.description: Memory impairment: memorizing a new telephone number is now beyond her; a shopping list cannot be kept in her mind; she may forget where she has placed her belongings.
Temper has got worse and she scolds her family members often.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Contribution to domestic chores is limited because such duty as mopping the floor would induce vertigo.

comparable_cases.case_name: Tsang Wai Ching v Iu Sau Ying (formerly trading under the business name of Cheong Shing Furniture Design Co)
comparable_cases.injury_description: Hit and fall case; plaintiff suffered headache, shoulder pain and vomiting. Diagnosis post-concussional syndrome. Scar at corner of left eye. 5 months sick leave and 1% impairment of whole body.

comparable_cases.case_name: Hung Shing Kun v Yeung Chi Ming & Anor
comparable_cases.injury_description: Assault case; plaintiff suffered head injury and episodes of blackout; residual pain over left shoulder, elbow, wrist and hand and gross deficit of muscle group on left upper limb.

comparable_cases.case_name: Chiu Wen Hsien v Tong Shuk Chung (formerly trading as Shun Tong Clearance and Repairs Construction Company & Others)
comparable_cases.injury_description: Workman hit at the head and right shoulder by a fallen brick; 10 cm laceration on head and deformed clavicle; complaints of residual pain, dizziness and vomiting.

comparable_cases.case_name: Chang Tsun Tein v Wai Lee Scaffolding Co Ltd
comparable_cases.injury_description: Workman hit by a bamboo pole at the head; 2 cm laceration of the scalp; complaints of dizziness, headache, inability to concentrate, loss of memory and impairment of psychological and social functioning. Award of $150,000.
